palette.model: Nord, with a warm paper interior
palette.grounds: Paper: a cool Nord canvas with a warm paper interior. Polar Night: Nord 0-3 throughout.
palette.relation: triad, 112 degrees between accent and masthead
palette.rule: The frame border is the temperature boundary: cool outside, warm inside, in the light theme only.

tokens.name: canvas
tokens.usage: The field the page floats on, and the ONLY cool thing in the Paper theme: Nord's deepest light tint outside, warm paper inside. The iceberg sits here at `wallpaper` strength, and it is cool because the berg is. Carries `ink` (9.72:1), `ink-soft` and `ink-dim` (4.80:1); NOT `accent` (4.17:1) or `dim` (3.87:1), and nothing should need text outside the frame anyway.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: The page container: warm paper in the Paper theme, Nord 0 in Polar Night. Ground for `ink` (13.18:1 / 10.84:1), `ink-soft`, `ink-dim`, `accent` (5.66:1 / 8.00:1) and `dim`.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Post cards, callouts, table headers. Carries every text token; the tightest pair is `dim` at 4.83:1 in Paper and 4.61:1 in Polar Night.

tokens.name: surface-nav
tokens.usage: The nav strip above and below the banner. Carries `ink`, `ink-soft`, `ink-dim`, `accent` (4.90:1 in Paper) and `dim` (4.54:1).

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Inline `code`, input wells, a table's total row. Carries every text token.

tokens.name: surface-mute
tokens.usage: Zebra rows, disabled controls, the shaded half of a comparison column. Carries `ink` and `ink-soft` ONLY: `dim` is 4.21:1 in Paper and 3.38:1 in Polar Night, and `ink-dim` is 4.07:1 in Polar Night.

tokens.name: code-surface
tokens.usage: Every code block: fenced blocks, terminal blocks and the home page shell well. The page's own sunken ground in both themes, so code repaints with the room instead of sitting as a dark slab on the paper.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Body copy, headings, nav labels. A warm near-black in Paper, Nord 6 in Polar Night. Clears 4.5:1 on every surface token and on `canvas`.

tokens.name: ink-soft
tokens.usage: Blockquotes, post descriptions, secondary prose. Legible on every ground including `surface-mute` and `canvas`.

tokens.name: ink-dim
tokens.usage: Dates, captions, footer text, table units. Legible on `surface`, `surface-raised`, `surface-nav`, `surface-sunken` and, in Paper, `canvas` (4.80:1). NOT on `surface-mute` in Polar Night (4.07:1).

tokens.name: code-ink
tokens.usage: Code text on `code-surface`; follows `ink` in both themes.

tokens.name: code-accent
tokens.usage: The shell prompt `$` and a highlighted line INSIDE `code-surface`. In Paper, Nord's Aurora purple held at 47% lightness so it still reads as purple next to `ink` (4.85:1 on the sunken ground); Aurora yellow in Polar Night.

tokens.name: code-dim
tokens.usage: Comments, terminal title bars and unimportant output inside `code-surface`; follows `ink-dim`.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: The single accent: links, active nav, section numbers, prose headings, an affirmative mark in a table. Aurora yellow `#ebcb8b` as Nord ships it on the dark ground (8.00:1), and the same hue driven to 28% lightness on the warm light one (5.66:1). Aurora is designed for a dark ground and none of it can carry text on a light one unchanged.

tokens.name: accent-fill
tokens.usage: The same yellow as a ground rather than an ink: the current row, the selected variant, a hover highlight, a quiet chip. The dark tint is held at low saturation so it sits inside Nord's ramp rather than reading as a brown patch on the blue-greys. Always put `on-accent-fill` on it (7.71:1 / 7.52:1). This token carries most of the colour in the system; `accent` is used sparingly by comparison.

tokens.name: on-accent-fill
tokens.usage: Text and marks sitting on `accent-fill`: 7.71:1 in Paper, 7.52:1 in Polar Night. In Polar Night it is the same value as `accent`, because a deep tint takes the pale ink.

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text on a SOLID `accent` fill: tag badges, primary buttons, the active tab. 5.66:1 in Paper, 9.34:1 in Polar Night.

tokens.name: masthead
tokens.usage: The banner band, constant in both themes and the only element outside the yellow family. Nord's Aurora purple `#b48ead` driven down to 30% lightness, because the Nord value carries white at only 2.83:1 and cannot be a band. Carries `banner-ink` at 8.81:1.

tokens.name: banner-ink
tokens.usage: The site name and strapline on `masthead`.

tokens.name: banner-mark
tokens.usage: The pale purple subtitle line on `masthead`, 5.49:1. One line per banner; never a second chromatic element in the band.

tokens.name: dim
tokens.usage: The tone that stands in place of red: a missed rep, a stall, an unavailable option, a delete that is safe. It reads as less, not wrong. Legible on `surface` (5.24:1 / 5.72:1), `surface-raised`, `surface-nav` and `surface-sunken`; NOT on `surface-mute` or `canvas`.

tokens.name: rule
tokens.usage: The 2px hard frame: the container, the nav strip. It is also the temperature boundary, the line where the cool canvas stops and the warm page begins. 9.72:1 on `canvas` in Paper and 3.20:1 in Polar Night, clearing the 3:1 floor for a meaningful border in both.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Decorative hairlines only: table cells, the divider under a post card, `<hr>`. Nord 2 in Polar Night. Never the sole indicator of a boundary that matters.

tokens.name: plate
tokens.usage: The panel an ornament sits on, constant across themes so a 1997 GIF looks the same on both grounds. A cool silver, which puts it on the canvas's side of the temperature split rather than the page's. Only `on-plate` goes on it.

tokens.name: on-plate
tokens.usage: Captions on `plate`, 9.10:1. A theme-swapping ink would go illegible on a constant silver, which is why this token exists.

styles.name: banner-title
styles.usage: The site name in the banner band. Drops to 28px below 800px.

styles.name: banner-sub
styles.usage: The gold subtitle line under the name, in `banner-mark`. Drops to 20px below 800px.

styles.name: nav
styles.usage: Nav labels in the strip. Courier keeps the chrome visibly older than the content.

styles.name: display
styles.usage: The h1 of a post or page, in `accent`.

styles.name: heading
styles.usage: Section heads, archive years, page titles. Pair with a section number set in `spec-label`.

styles.name: subhead
styles.usage: h3 inside prose and on the home page, in `accent`.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Callout labels and eyebrow text. Set it uppercase in CSS; the letterspacing is what makes uppercase mono readable.

styles.name: meta
styles.usage: Post dates, breadcrumbs, table units, in `ink-dim`.

styles.name: caption
styles.sample: A short description of the post.
styles.usage: Post descriptions and figure captions, in `ink-soft`.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Long-form paragraphs set in the same face as everything else.
styles.usage: Every paragraph, list item and table cell in an article, and the body of a callout. IBM Plex Mono at 15px and 1.7 leading. `measure-prose` is 80ch, which in a monospace face is exactly 80 characters: a terminal's width, about 720px.

styles.name: quote
styles.usage: Blockquotes, in `ink-soft`, behind a 4px `accent` left rule. Italic monospace is unusual and that is the point: a quote should look like an interruption.

styles.name: metric
styles.usage: The one number a card exists to show: a working weight, a spec headline. `signal` is legible at this size in both themes.

styles.name: figure
styles.usage: Numbers inside a table or a set row. JetBrains Mono because these sit in columns under one another.

styles.name: figure-sm
styles.usage: Dense spec values and secondary figures.

styles.name: spec-label
styles.usage: Section numbers and spec-table column heads. Set uppercase in CSS.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Gap between a post title and its date; list item padding.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: The banner's own padding and a nav link's padding. Kept at 5px rather than snapped to the grid, because that is what the site is.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Tag badge horizontal padding; gap inside a callout header.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Container padding, nav strip padding, footer padding. The default inset of the frame.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Gutter on mobile; gap between spec table rows.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Vertical margin between the container and the viewport edge.

tokens.name: space-7
tokens.usage: Space below a post card; margin above a callout.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Page content and prose padding on desktop, and the side gutter around the frame. The main breathing step.

tokens.name: space-9
tokens.usage: Gap between the two items in the post nav; space above a numbered section.

radius.note: Soft corners, hard borders: still no shadows. The frame is the roundest thing on the page so everything inside nests.

tokens.name: radius-0
tokens.usage: The frame and its bands on mobile, where the frame fills the screen.

tokens.name: radius-xs
tokens.usage: Small things: tag badges, the copy button, inline `code`, link and nav hover highlights.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Blocks: code and terminal blocks, the shell well, callouts, images in prose, the ornament plate, data rows, mobile menu items.

tokens.name: radius-frame
tokens.usage: The container frame on desktop. It clips the banner band and nav strips to its corners.

tokens.name: radius-disc
tokens.usage: The theme toggle and nothing else.

border.note: The system draws separation with borders, never with shadows. There is no shadow family on purpose.

tokens.name: border-hair
tokens.usage: Table cells, card dividers, inline code, `<hr>`, in `line`.

tokens.name: border-hard
tokens.usage: The container frame, the nav strip's top and bottom, every image in prose, the focus ring, in `rule`.

tokens.name: border-mark
tokens.usage: A callout's left edge, in the callout's own tone.

tokens.name: border-quote
tokens.usage: A blockquote's left edge, in `accent`.

measure.note: Three widths; nothing else is a layout constant.

tokens.name: measure-frame
tokens.usage: The container, with a `space-8` gutter either side until the viewport is wide enough. Below 800px it goes full width, loses its side borders and its corners.

tokens.name: measure-prose
tokens.usage: The reading column inside the frame, for `body`: 80 characters of mono, about 720px at 15px.

tokens.name: measure-wide
tokens.usage: Full-bleed sections: spec tables, galleries, the CV grid.

opacity.note: Two veils, both measured against the iceberg image rather than guessed.

tokens.name: veil
tokens.usage: The strength of the iceberg ghost INSIDE the frame, over `surface`. Measured: at 0.06 the weakest token, `dim`, still holds 4.63:1 in Paper and 6.02:1 in CRT across the whole image. At 0.08 `dim` drops to 4.43:1 and fails. Do not raise it.

tokens.name: wallpaper
tokens.usage: The iceberg on `canvas` behind the frame runs at full strength, because `canvas` carries no text. In CRT it takes `background-blend-mode: multiply` against the near-black so it reads as the same berg at night.
